Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a dense opacity in the right upper lobe that respects the fissure without significant volume loss, a presentation characteristic of mucinous pulmonary adenocarcinoma (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma) which can mimic lobar pneumonia but lacks the acute infectious signs or rapid resolution. While infectious pneumonia is a differential, the specific description of fissure-respecting consolidation with preserved volume in this context strongly points towards this malignancy subtype.
